speaker_role: college admissions coach/consultant (InGenius Prep); relaying secondhand claims attributed to unnamed former admissions officers from Dartmouth, Brown, Johns Hopkins, Bowdoin, UChicago, and Michigan
commercial_incentive: InGenius Prep sells admissions coaching services; episode promotes free consultations
key_insights: Legacy status can give an edge at elite schools, but each school defines it differently (e.g. Princeton counts only parents/stepparents as legacy)
Buying admission via large donations doesn't reliably work for typical donors; scrutiny increased after the Varsity Blues scandal
Stereotyped extracurriculars (JV sports, generic volunteering) aren't disqualifying if the student is genuinely and sincerely engaged
A high SAT/ACT score alone doesn't guarantee admission; GPA and course rigor matter more, and scores may hit a 'threshold' beyond which more points stop helping
Some colleges are 'need-aware' and can factor ability to pay into admission; most elite/Ivy-caliber schools are need-blind for domestic applicants
A perfect GPA isn't required; admissions officers want rigor and evidence of bouncing back from occasional dips, especially outside junior/senior year
Demonstrated interest reportedly matters more at schools just below the very top tier (e.g. WashU, Williams, Tufts) and can be shown via info sessions, tours, and consistent contact email use
Being 'well-rounded' is described as outdated; colleges are said to now prefer specialists/'spike' students who show depth in one or two areas
specific_numbers_or_facts: Stanford is said to consider families capable of donating $500,000+ as 'big donors' (per Poto/InGenius)
Princeton legacy definition cited as limited to parent/stepparent alumni only (per Poto/InGenius)
notable_or_distinctive: Frames advice as a consensus gathered specifically from former admissions officers at six named schools, including an explicit case where those officers disagreed (whether volunteering is required).
reliability_notes: Claims are secondhand and unverifiable (no individual officers or dates named); some sales framing toward InGenius Prep's coaching services; transcript is otherwise clean.
